transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-28
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyer (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Diane Cole (Brightline Procurement), Ravi Patel (Brightline CISO), Laura Nguyen (Brightline Cloud Eng), Marta Gomez (Brightline Legal)

Summary: Initial procurement/legal review to align on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations, pricing tiers for a pilot, and onboarding steps for a VPC-based pilot. Some technical clarifications on data residency, KMS, and SOC2. Action items and next steps captured at the end.

Topics: MSA redlines, DPA/processing scope, SLA/latency SLOs, SOC2/pen test, VPC/on-prem onboarding, pricing/committed tiers, timeline for pilot and legal review.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we really appreciate you taking the time. Quick roll call so I know we've got the right folks: Diane, Ravi, Laura, Marta?
[00:06] Diane (Brightline - Procurement): Hi Jordan, hi Priya. Yep Diane here.
[00:08] Ravi (Brightline - CISO): Ravi here.
[00:10] Laura (Brightline - Cloud Eng): Laura here, thanks.
[00:12] Marta (Brightline - Legal): Marta here.
[00:14] Priya (Redwood - SE): Great, thanks all. We'll run for about 45-60 minutes and focus on the MSA/DPA redline items, SLA expectations, and the pilot onboarding steps.
[00:24] Jordan: Quick agenda — legal clarifications first, pricing then, and technical onboarding last. Sound good?
[00:27] Diane: That works. Procurement is primarily focused on DPA scope and the liability caps in the MSA, then we need to see pricing for a 3-month pilot with a committed throughput.
[00:35] Jordan: Understood. Priya, want to start with how we handle data, residency, and the DPA?
[00:40] Priya: Sure; so Redwood's standard DPA covers processing for inference requests, we offer options for data retention controls — default ephemeral retention and an opt-in for logging for debugging. For Brightline's case we recommend VPC private deployment or dedicated if you need strict isolation.
[00:55] Ravi: On retention — we need confirmation that PHI is never written to persistent logs and that encryption-at-rest keys are under our KMS. Can you support a customer-managed KMS/HSM?
[01:05] Priya: Yes, we support bring-your-own KMS for Private deployments; for Hosted we have envelope encryption with customer-managed keys available for Enterprise accounts. There was a... um, note about HSM integrations, we do have partners for HSM integration — we can share the KMS/HSM matrix.
[01:20] Ravi: Okay, and what about audit logs and access controls? We need audit-forwarding to our SIEM.
[01:27] Priya: We can stream audit logs to your S3 or to a SIEM; there's an audit-log webhook as well. RBAC and SSO via SAML2 is supported. Small note: sometimes Fireflies transcription says SAML1 or Saml2, but it's SAML2 really.
[01:40] Diane: From procurement — the MSA has a standard 1M liability cap which is below our threshold, we usually need 5M for critical vendors. Is there flexibility?
[01:48] Jordan: We can take that back to legal, generally we have tiers tied to platform commitments and revenue-based caps; for enterprise deals we can discuss increasing liability or adding insurance. Would that be sufficient to meet your policy?
[02:00] Marta: We'll need to see insurance certificates and indemnity language. Also, Brightline prefers redline-friendly documents — can you send both clean and redline MSA/DPA copies?
[02:09] Jordan: Absolutely, we'll send both. We'll include SOC2 Type II report and latest pen test summary.
[02:14] Ravi: Pen test summary ok, but we may need the full report under NDA — we can sign an NDA if needed.
[02:19] Jordan: Yep, we can share under an NDA.
[02:22] Priya: On SLAs — we typically offer latency SLOs for hosted models and more strict SLOs for Dedicated. For example, our hosted baseline is 99.5% for <500ms p50 and 95% for p95 with model-dependent variance; Dedicated can be SLA-backed with per-route SLOs and dedicated GPU pools.
[02:44] Laura: Do you have example numbers for the models we'll likely use? Our primary workload is clinical triage prompts, sequence lengths average 1k tokens.
[02:52] Priya: For 1k tokens we usually see higher tail latencies — our benchmark sheet has model-by-length tables. For a medium-sized LlamaX variant on Dedicated, p50 might be 350ms, p95 ~700-900ms depending on batch; on Hosted it's a bit higher due to multi-tenant scheduling. We'll share the benchmark CSV.
[03:10] Diane: For the pilot procurement, pricing is the key unblock — we need committed capacity pricing and an overage rate.
[03:17] Jordan: We'll provide a committed-tier pricing sheet — typically we do a pilot discount (20-30% off list) for a 3-month commit. If you convert to Dedicated reserve after pilot we offer step-down per-token pricing with commit tiers.
[03:29] Marta: Legal will also want data residency guarantees in the DPA — EU/US regions, do you geo-fence?
[03:35] Priya: Yes, requests can be routed regionally and we offer region pinning for customer tenants. For Private deployments you control the region entirely.
[03:42] Ravi: Can you confirm data deletion procedures, certs after deletion? We need verifiable deletion for certain PHI types.
[03:48] Priya: We can provide deletion manifests for Private and Dedicated deployments; for Hosted we can provide deletion confirmations and logs showing retention removal. There's sometimes a small delay depending on caching and KV cache eviction — we call it KV cash in some notes, but it's KV cache evict.
[04:02] Laura: On onboarding — what does the VPC peering setup look like? Who roots the peering?
[04:07] Priya: For VPC we have a runbook: you share network ranges, we set up peering and route tables from our side, and you approve. We'll provide terraform snippets.
[04:16] Laura: Will there be ip allowlists and static egress? We need to lock down egress to our SIEM endpoints.
[04:21] Priya: Yep static IP egress and allowlist options exist for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted there are NAT egress ranges we can provide.
[04:29] Diane: What about compliance artifacts — SOC2, ISO, DPIA?
[04:33] Jordan: We'll attach SOC2 Type II, summary of ISO controls, and our DPA includes DPIA mappings for healthcare. Full DPIA is doable on request.
[04:41] Marta: On indemnity, we prefer carveouts for customer-supplied data — we need clear language that customer is responsible for input data accuracy and PHI compliance.
[04:48] Jordan: That's standard — we'll flag that clause.
[04:51] Priya: For the pilot we recommend a small dedicated pool or private tenant so you can validate latency and isolation. Typical pilot config is 2 gpus reserved for 3 months with a burst pool.
[05:05] Laura: What's the expected monthly token volume for that?
[05:07] Priya: For triage, rough ballpark 30M tokens/month per app, but depends on concurrency. We'll need your usage profile.
[05:15] Laura: We'll send sample traffic patterns.
[05:18] Diane: Pricing question — do you support PO-based invoicing and net-45?
[05:22] Jordan: Yes enterprise invoicing with PO is supported; payment terms usually net-30 standard, but net-45 is possible on request and sometimes tied to contract terms.
[05:31] Marta: (laughs) Marta — typo in call notes —
[05:33] Marta (Brightline Legal): Sorry, just noting procurement tends to push net-45.
[05:36] Jordan: We can be flexible — we'll propose net-45 in the pricing doc for procurement.
[05:40] Ravi: One more security ask — can Redwood rotate keys on customer schedule and provide KMS access logs?
[05:45] Priya: Yes; for BYOK KMS we don't have access to plaintext keys, we can rotate per customer schedule and provide KMS access metrics.
[05:52] Diane: On timeline — procurement wants to finish legal review within two weeks. Is that realistic?
[05:56] Jordan: If we get redlines today we can turn around a counter within 3-5 business days; sharing SOC2 and pen test will speed it. Pilot onboarding can begin after contracts are signed and the PO is issued.
[06:08] Laura: For onboarding, what support level will be provided? 
[06:11] Priya: We include onboarding with an SE-led session, runbooks, and 2 weeks of hypercare for pilots. For Dedicated there's also an implementation engineer option.
[06:20] Jordan: I'll also include a contact list and escalation matrix.
[06:23] Diane: Great. A few small items: 1) we need SLA credit language spelled out, 2) want pricing floor for conversion to dedicated, 3) can you provide a sample MSA with our typical redlines pre-applied so our legal can see changes quickly.
[06:38] Jordan: We'll do that — sample MSA with redlines + a redline-friendly doc. SLA credit language we have standard templates for, we'll include.
[06:45] Priya: Also note that fallback policies exist — if Dedicated capacity is constrained we can route to compatible family models — but for PHI workloads we recommend Private/Dedicated to avoid multi-tenant routing.
[06:58] Ravi: That routing fallback is a concern. We need a strict control that PHI never routes off your dedicated tenant.
[07:05] Priya: Understood — for Dedicated we can add an explicit no-fallback clause for PHI-tagged routes. We'll propose the clause for the DPA/MSA.
[07:14] Diane: Ok that helps.
[07:17] Jordan: Any other open items before we wrap?
[07:19] Marta: Legal will review the indemnity and liability cap and get back. We will need to set a time for the legal-only call.
[07:26] Jordan: Let's tentatively aim for week of Apr 6. I'll send a poll.
[07:30] Laura: We'll get the sample traffic and a data inventory to you by Apr 2.
[07:34] Ravi: And I'll review the KMS/HSM matrix once you send it.
[07:38] Jordan: Perfect. We'll follow up with the MSA/DPA, SOC2, pen test summary, pricing sheet, and a proposed SLA language.
[07:47] Diane: Thanks everyone.
[07:48] Jordan: Thanks all — talk soon.

Recap / Next Steps (verbatim):
- Jordan to send redline-friendly MSA/DPA bundle and SOC2 + pen test summary (due 2026-04-02)
- Priya to share benchmark spreadsheet, SLA language examples, and VPC onboarding runbook (due 2026-04-01 / 2026-04-03)
- Jordan to send committed-tier pricing spreadsheet and pilot invoice example (due 2026-04-03)
- Brightline to provide sample traffic profiles and data inventory (owner: Laura; due 2026-04-02)
- Schedule legal-only review week of 2026-04-06 (owner: Marta)

Notes on transcription quality: medium — occasional mis-typed acronyms (e.g., KV cash vs KV cache), speaker overlaps, and minor word swaps.

References shared: Pricing spreadsheet (link placeholder), MSA/DPA draft (to be sent), SOC2 Type II report (to be sent under NDA), VPC runbook (to be shared by Priya).

End of transcript.
